rounds.proof_sketch: Model uses affine=True (default). Dispatch checks `if (weight.defined() && bias.defined())` → always TRUE. Calls instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine (unmutated). The mutated instance_norm_forward_kernel is in the else branch → NEVER executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation is located in `instance_norm_forward_kernel`, the non-affine kernel variant. However, `InstanceNorm2dCustom` is instantiated with `affine=True` (the default), which means `self.weight` and `self.bias` are always created as Parameters. The CUDA dispatch logic `if (weight.defined() && bias.defined())` therefore always evaluates to true, routing all calls to `instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine`, which does NOT contain the mutation. The mutated loop `i <= spatial_size` in the non-affine kernel is dead code under this configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed contract. Would require changing model configuration to affine=False, which violates the testing contract. The mutation is in unreachable code because the dispatch predicate always selects the unmutated affine kernel.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing should track code coverage to identify mutations in unreachable code paths. This mutation in the non-affine kernel path provides zero coverage when testing with affine=True configuration. Either (1) mark such mutations as equivalent under the fixed configuration, or (2) ensure mutation targets are in code paths actually exercised by the test harness.
